key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the dying declaration made by the victim to PW-6 (Dr. Langkumer) and PW-7 (Nabanita Barauh), which was corroborated by PW-1 and PW-8.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of PW-6 and PW-7 as reliable witnesses, noting they were not related to the victim, not interested witnesses, and their statements were fully corroborated by other witnesses.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: not stated; Trial judgment: 30.03.2006; High Court decision: 20.03.2007; Supreme Court decision: 04.09.2014
legal_representation: P.K. Goswami, Parthiv K. Goswami, A. Henry, Rajiv Mehta for the Appellant; Avijit Roy for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: conviction and sentence; High Court: affirmed conviction and sentence; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant-accused poured kerosene oil on his wife and set her on fire, leading to her death. The evidence included two dying declarations from the victim, corroborated by witnesses, and the victim's death was attributed to burn injuries.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the dying declaration made by the victim was unreliable, as it was an oral statement and there was no smell of kerosene oil on the victim's body. They also cited the case of Surinder Kumar v. State of Haryana to challenge the admissibility of the dying declaration.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a dying declaration is admissible if it is corroborated by other evidence and the circumstances surrounding its making are not suspicious.
precedent_relied_upon: Surinder Kumar v State of Haryana (2011) 10 SCC 173; State of Rajasthan vs. Kishore (1996) 8 SCR 217
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence of life imprisonment was imposed because the prosecution proved the case beyond all reasonable doubt, and the trial court and High Court found the appellant guilty under section 302 IPC.
